title: External motivation, the key to success in the MOOCs framework
reason: Moodle-recorded time spent in the LMS correlated with course points (r = 0.75) and with an external-motivation (course-credit) condition in a MOOC. Meets I1. Mixed sample including university students, so E3 not clearly applicable; flagged.

extraction.country: Serbia and Hungary (MOOC participants: 135 Serbia, 71 Hungary, 2 Romania)
extraction.design: correlational case study (Pearson r, t-tests, ANOVA)
extraction.n_quote: 208 students enrolled on this given course, in the following composition: 79% (165) female and 21% (43) male students
extraction.population: MOOC enrolees: 99 students, 86 teachers, 23 other; primary target group Hungarian secondary-school students in Serbia; 44 first/second-year university students (Novi Sad teacher training) received course credit
extraction.lms_indicators: time spent in the Moodle LMS (system-recorded)
extraction.outcome_or_construct: course achievement (points from assignments, forum, final test); 'external motivation' (receiving formal-course credit, self-reported at application)

effect_sizes.between: time spent in LMS ↔ course achievement (points), whole sample
effect_sizes.quote: between the amount of time spent in the LMS and student achievements - amount of acquired points (Pearson correlation factor r= 0.75, p= 0.001).

effect_sizes.between: time spent in LMS ↔ course achievement, active students only
effect_sizes.quote: the amount of time spent in the LMS and the variable of student achievements show a significant correlation (Pearson correlation factor = 0.46, p=0.001).

effect_sizes.between: external motivation ↔ time spent in LMS
effect_sizes.quote: External motivation and the variable of time spent in this framework demonstrated an apparent relationship (Pearson correlation factor=0.38, p=0.001).

effect_sizes.between: external motivation ↔ time spent in LMS, students who logged in
effect_sizes.quote: a statistically outstanding correlation emerges between the external motivation and time spent in LMS (Pearson correlation factor = 0.25, p= 0.003).

extraction.notes: E3 risk: sample is mixed (secondary-school students are the primary target group; 41% teachers); analyses pool all participants, HE students are 44/208. 'External motivation' is defined by the authors as course points transferable to formal education, i.e. an incentive condition, not a measured trait, so I2 is not claimed. Tables 3-5 are images; values taken from narrative text.
